items.stem: Which of the following is a way to describe the concentration of a solution quantitatively?
What is the mole fraction of a component in a solution?
What is the mass percentage of a component in a solution?
If 20 g of ethylene glycol is dissolved in 80 g of water, what is the mole fraction of ethylene glycol in the solution?
What is the molality of a solution containing 2.5 g of ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) in 75 g of benzene?
What is the molarity of a solution containing 5 g of NaOH in 450 mL solution?
If the Henry’s law constant for N₂ at 293 K is 76.48 kbar, and the partial pressure of N₂ is 0.987 bar, what is the mole fraction of N₂ in the solution?
According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to which of the following?
What does Raoult's law state about the partial vapour pressure of a component in a solution?
In the context of Henry’s law, what is the significance of the slope of the graph between the partial pressure of the gas and the mole fraction of the gas in the solution?
If a non-volatile solute is added to a solvent, what happens to the vapour pressure of the solution?
Why does the vapour phase become richer in the more volatile component?
Which law states that the vapour pressure of a solvent in a solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction?
In a solution where the vapour pressure is higher than predicted by Raoult’s law, what type of deviation is observed?
In a solution of two volatile liquids, how is the total vapour pressure calculated?
If a solution shows a large positive deviation from Raoult’s law, what type of mixture is formed?
Why do some solutions show negative deviations from Raoult’s law?
If the density of lake water is 1.25 g/mL and it contains 92 g of Na+ ions per kg of water, what is the molarity of Na+ ions in the lake?
If the osmotic pressure of a solution is 1.52 bars at 300 K, what would be its concentration if 36 g of glucose in a litre of solution has an osmotic pressure of 4.98 bars?
What is a solution?
If a solution contains 10% w/w glucose, what is the mass of glucose in 200 g of solution?
What is the mass percentage of aspirin (C9H8O4) in acetonitrile (CH3CN) when 6.5 g of aspirin is dissolved in 450 g of acetonitrile?
What is the van’t Hoff factor and dissociation constant of fluoroacetic acid if 19.5 g of CH2FCOOH is dissolved in 500 g of water and the depression in freezing point is 1.0°C? (Kf = 1.86 K kg/mol)
What is the effect of a non-volatile solute on the vapour pressure of a solvent?
A 68% nitric acid solution has a density of 1.504 g mL⁻¹. What is the molarity of this solution?
What happens to the experimentally determined molar mass when there is dissociation of solute into ions?
A solution of 2% non-volatile solute exerts a pressure of 1.004 bar at the normal boiling point of the solvent. What is the molar mass of the solute?
In the case of association of molecules, what is the value of the van't Hoff factor (i)?
What is the main advantage of using osmotic pressure to determine molar mass of solutes?
If the freezing point depression of a solution is 1.62 K and the molal depression constant of benzene is 4.9 K kg mol⁻¹, what is the van't Hoff factor (i) for benzoic acid in benzene?
A solution containing 1.26 g of protein in 200 cm³ of water has an osmotic pressure of 2.57 × 10⁻³ bar at 300 K. What is the molar mass of the protein?
What is the term used to describe the lowering of the freezing point of a solvent when a non-volatile solute is added?
Why does the solubility of gases in liquids decrease with an increase in temperature?
Which of the following is an example of a liquid solution?
What is the definition of molarity?
What is the definition of molality?
What is the key factor that determines whether a solute dissolves in a solvent?
If the dissolution of a solid is endothermic, how does the solubility change with an increase in temperature?
What is the purpose of applying excess pressure on the solution side in reverse osmosis?
